verdict: Iran peace deal + MU blowout Q3 guide ($33.5B/81% GM) + DRAM supercycle intact; HBM 2027 re-pricing stalling higher — near-term semi bull case strengthens.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments — last 24-72h

**Macro (June 15):** US-Iran peace deal confirmed; Strait of Hormuz to reopen. Oil futures -4.8% (WTI ~$80.83). Asian equities surged (Kospi +5.1%, Nikkei +3.6%), driving a broad risk-on rally into semiconductors/growth names.

**Signal 1 — DRAM pricing (TrendForce, June 1-2):** Q1 2026 DRAM industry revenue +81% QoQ. Q2 2026 contract prices guided +58–63% QoQ. Historic crossover: DDR5 64GB RDIMM profitability **exceeded HBM3e** in Q1 2026 for the first time; HBM current (2026) contract prices pressured by rigid annual-pricing mechanism.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 / 2027 re-pricing (TrendForce, June 2 + June 9):** 2027 HBM contract talks **stalling** — suppliers demanding prices "multiple times higher" vs current, citing NVIDIA Rubin Ultra (384 GB/GPU), ASIC volume growth, and manufacturing complexity. This materially **contradicts** the "correction after 2026" baseline thesis: the correction (profitability dip) is in *2026*, while 2027 looks like a re-price to the upside. SK Hynix HBM4 ramp pushed from Q2 → Q3 2026 (HBM3e demand too strong to idle capacity early). Micron HBM4: on track, supply sold out through 2026.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler capex:** No fresh prints this week. Big-4 aggregate stands at ~$725B for 2026 (+77% YoY). No guide-down.

**Signal 4 — Custom ASIC / AMD:** No fresh MI400/Helios news. Marvell launched **Teralynx T100** (June 1) — first 102.4 Tbps AI-native switch, 3nm, CPO-option — strengthening MRVL custom-silicon/networking story.

**Signal 5 — Optical (June 10):** LITE +5%, COHR +2%, AAOI +7% as optics group rides AI infrastructure momentum. JPMorgan reiterated Buy on both COHR and LITE. Credo (CRDO) completed acquisition of DustPhotonics (May 2026), adding 800G–3.2T silicon photonics. CPO deployment timeline still 2028–2030; pluggables dominant near-term.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** No fresh module-pricing data this week. Solar stocks +40% YTD; Section 232 tariff decision still pending (key risk/catalyst). No fresh FSLR/ENPH/NXT/ARRY name-specific news in the 24-72h window.

---

## Context vs. Baseline

The "correction after 2026" HBM thesis appears **earlier and shallower** than feared: the profitability dip is happening in 2026 (HBM margins below DDR5), but 2027 re-pricing is heading higher, not lower, as demand from Rubin Ultra and ASICs outpaces new capacity. Hyperscaler capex running 15-20% above the baseline $600-700B estimate. Optical demand structural; supply gap persists.

---

| Hyperscaler capex ($725B, no guide-down) | ↑ | Bull |
| AMD MI400 / custom ASIC share-shift | → | Neutral (no new data) |
| Optical (LITE/COHR/CRDO rallying; Teralynx CPO-ready) | ↑ | Bull |
| Solar (40% YTD; S232 looming) | → | Neutral/watch |
| Watchlist movers (MU +8%, broad rally) | ↑ | Bull |

---

## Most Important Development

**MU pre-earnings +8% on a Q3 guide of $33.5B revenue / 81% gross margin** (reports June 24) is the sharpest near-term catalyst in the watchlist. Combined with TrendForce's June 9 HBM 2027 update (talks stalling, prices set to surge "multiples"), the correction-after-2026 fear is being replaced by a 2027 re-pricing bull case. The US-Iran deal is a meaningful macro tailwind today.
